question: Around 36 % of the territory of the Republic of Cyprus, an EU Member State, has been illegally occupied by Türkiye since the Turkish invasion of 1974. Around one in three nativeborn Greek Cypriots – i.e.

180 000 – were expelled from their native land, leaving behind their homes and properties located in Turkish-occupied Northern Cyprus, which, according to numerous ECHR decisions, has ever since been controlled by an occupation regime subordinate to Türkiye. Since then, they have been living as refugees in Southern Cyprus, which remains under the control of the Republic of Cyprus.

For some time now, Greek Cypriot properties have been illegally purchased and sold – including by citizens of EU Member States, with advertisements placed in many of these countries – with the encouragement of the occupation regime and without the consent of the legal owners. The matter has been internationally denounced by the authorities of the Republic of Cyprus1234.

In light of the above, what measures does the Commission intend to take and what measures will it recommend Member States take in order to put a stop to the illegal purchase of Greek Cypriot properties by EU citizens, which is against international and EU law, and the illegal advertising of this inadmissible practice within the EU?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.2.2025) Article 7 of Council Regulation (EC) No 389/2006 (the Aid Regulation)1 provides that the Commission shall ensure that in the implementation of actions financed under the Regulation the rights of natural or legal persons, including the rights to possessions and property, are respected.
To this end, the Commission systematically consults the authorities of the Republic of Cyprus to avoid infringing property rights by such actions.

Outside the scope of the Aid Regulation, the Commission has no competence to ensure that property transactions in the non-government-controlled areas respect the rights of the owners concerned, due to the suspension of the acquis in those areas pursuant to Protocol 10 of the 2003 Act of Accession2.

The Commission is aware of civil cases decided by courts of the Republic of Cyprus against EU citizens involved in illegal property transactions and property developments in the areas not under the effective control of the government of the Republic of Cyprus. All courts of the Member States are obliged to comply with the judgment of the Grand Chamber in the Case C420/07 Apostolides v Orams3.
